Duration values are immutable tagged records with own u64 BigInt seconds and normalized u32 BigInt nanoseconds below 1000000000; private fields describe the lowering ABI, not source-level constructor permission. Checked operations return frozen Rust Option values; ordinary operation overflow and invalid float constructors abort as Rust panics, never synthetic successful Results. Source f64 conversions preserve IEEE-754 values and nearest-nanosecond ties-to-even; f32 contracts are omitted until the frontend distinguishes binary32. constEligible means the pinned source declares the function const; pure alone never grants const evaluation to trait or floating constructor methods. Source-derived fixtures establish the adapter subset; Rust differential execution stays gated on complete JavaScript checks.
Rust primitive, array and algebraic arguments are validated recursively; strings contain Unicode scalars, fixed integers are BigInt and in range
trim uses Unicode White_Space; ASCII folds preserve non-ASCII scalars; len uses UTF-8 bytes and chars().count uses Unicode scalars

The actual checked fixed-integer target, signedness and width determine this monomorphic parser and Result layout. Decimal FromStr accepts an optional ASCII plus sign, and signed targets also accept minus; no whitespace trimming or JavaScript numeric coercion is introduced. Invalid digits are checked before reporting multiplication overflow at that byte; a preceding digit overflow stops before any later invalid byte. Machine integers remain BigInt; usize/isize aliases use the existing checked 64-bit portable profile. FromStr and str.parse are not const-eligible; stable from_str_radix is const-eligible since Rust 1.82, with invalid radix preserving source panic behavior. NonZero types, binary32/binary64 FromStr, generic unbound parse targets and unchecked mutation require separate contracts. No Rust execution or complete Router parity is established by these source-derived adapters.
every natural, integer and machine integer is a BigInt; machine-integer results are range-checked and throw RangeError where Rust would panic
